name: Holden Spaht
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Holden Spaht is a managing partner of software-focused private-equity firm Thoma Bravo, which ranks among the world's top buyout investors.
The firm, with assets of $181 billion, was formed in 2008, when Orlando Bravo and Carl Thoma split from partner Brian Cressey, who was focused on healthcare deals.
Spaht, a Dartmouth graduate and Harvard MBA, has led many of the firm's application software investments.
He joined Thoma Bravo in 2005 after stints at Thomas H. Lee Partners and Morgan Stanley Capital Partners.
His family foundation, founded with his wife Claire in 2019, supports mental health, environmental conservation and the arts.
forbes_facts: Spath, who was born and raised in Baton Rouge, describes himself as a ?rabid LSU football fan.?
The Spaht Family Foundation is the lead donor for Washington & Lee's Lindley Center, a health and counseling clinic named for his late sister, Dr. Lindley Spaht.

name: Giorgio Perfetti
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2004-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Giorgio Perfetti and his brother Augusto own candy and gum giant Perfetti Van Melle, a private company with more than $4.8 billion in revenues in 2024.
His father Ambrogio and uncle Egidio started the company in 1946 as a chewing gum business in a small town near Milan.
In 2022, the company announced it would acquire Mondelez International's developed market gum business, adding brands such as Trident, Dentyne and Bubbalicious.
The company's top-selling brands include Mentos and Airheads.
Perfetti once sold a 300-foot yacht under construction to fellow billionaire Suleiman Kerimov.
forbes_facts: Perfetti's father and uncle were inspired to start the company after seeing American soldiers bring gum to Europe during World War II.
Giorgio Perfetti reportedly owns one of the world's most renowned Ferrari car collections, including a much-coveted 1962 250 GTO.

name: Julio Ponce Lerou
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Julio Ponce Lerou owns a 17% stake in Sociedad de Quimica y Minera de Chile (SQM), a publicly-traded chemicals and mining company.
He resigned as chairman of SQM in 2015, citing personal reasons.
SQM is one of the world's largest miners of lithium, which is used in batteries for electric cars.
For almost 40 years Ponce headed SQM, which also mines and sells potassium nitrate and iodine -- chemicals used in fertilizers.
He is a former son-in-law of the late Chilean dictator Augusto Pinochet, and SQM was privatized by Pinochet's government in the 1980s.

name: Pavel Baudis
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: In 1988 software engineer Pavel Baudis wrote his first antivirus program after a friend sent him a floppy disk containing the "Vienna" computer virus.
In April that year, he and Eduard Kucera, with whom he'd worked at Research Institute of Mathematical Machines, cofounded ALWIL to sell the software.
Following the fall of Communism in 1989, the pair broke off to establish what would become Avast.
Now run by an outside CEO, Avast, which secures online activities for more than 435 million users, went public in 2018.
Its goals for the future are loftier: to protect all things in your home connected to the internet, from thermostats to webcams.

name: Li Gaiteng
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Hurun China (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: Li Gaiteng is the founder and chairman of Shanghai Flyco Electrical Appliance, a maker of personal care appliances such as electric razors and hair dryers.
His wife Lin Yu'e is an executive director at Flyco, which is majority owned by Li.
Li started the business after working as a motorcycle repairman.

name: Shlomo Kramer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Shlomo Kramer is cofounder and CEO of Cato Networks, a cloud security startup last valued by investors in 2021 at $2.5 billion.
He cofounded Check Point Software, a firewall security pioneer, with fellow Israelis Gil Shwed and Marius Nacht in 1993. Check Point went public in 1996.
Kramer cofounded data security company Imperva in 2002; it went public in 2011 and was acquired by Thoma Bravo in 2019 for about $2.1 billion.
Kramer was an early investor and board member at cybersecurity company Palo Alto Networks, founded by former Check Point employee Nir Zuk.
He has also invested in sales software maker Gong, cybersecurity company Exabeam and cloud data company Sumo Logic.

name: Dermot Desmond
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2006-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Dermot Desmond started his career in finance at Citibank, and later worked for the Investment Bank of Ireland and PricewaterhouseCoopers.
In 1981 he founded NCB Stockbrokers, which became Ireland's largest independent brokerage; he sold it for $39 million in 1994.
With the proceeds, Desmond started his own private equity firm, International Investment & Underwriting.
IIU now has stakes in travel software firm Datalex, Mountain Province Diamonds, Barchester Healthcare and Glasgow soccer club Celtic PLC.
forbes_facts: An avid golfer, he's known as "The Kaiser" for his distinctive mustache.
He also owns stakes in two luxury hotels in the Caribbean, the Pink Sands Club and the Sandy Lane Hotel.

name: Walter Wang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: Walter Wang is chairman and CEO of JM Eagle Inc., one of the world's largest manufacturers of plastic pipe.
Wang is a son of Y.C. Wang, the former chairman of Taiwan's Formosa Plastics, who died in 2008 at age 91.
Headquartered in Los Angeles, JM Eagle has 2,000 employees globally and generates $2.3 billion of estimated annual revenue.
Wang's philanthropic interests include healthcare, education and missionary work.
Wang is the founder and owner of a Taiwanese basketball team, the New Taipei Kings. His daughter named the team after the family name Wang, which means king in Mandarin.
forbes_facts: Wang survived a battle with nasopharynx cancer in 2005, which he credits to his Christian faith.

name: Luciano Hang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Brazil's Luciano Hang has found success with department store chain Havan by focusing heavily on physical stores rather than online sales.
Hang cofounded Havan in 1986; today it employs approximately 20,000 people in over 150 locations.
Hang bought out his cofounder early on and today owns nearly all of Havan, which had about $1.9 billion in 2020 revenues.
Hang has many followers on social media; he regularly live streams about politics on Facebook and gets up to 1 million views.
Hang is a vocal supporter of Brazil's President Jair Bolsonaro, a right-wing candidate who was elected in October 2018.

name: Megdet Rahimkulov
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021-2025); Forbes annual (2008-2022); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: In the mid-1990s Rahimkulov became chief executive and 10% owner of a joint venture between gas giant Gazprom and Hungary's oil and gas concern MOL.
He also headed AEB, a Hungarian bank that Gazprom bought to process payments from its local customers; he later bought it from Gazprom.
In 2007 he sold the bank and used the proceeds to buy shares in MOL and OTP, Hungary's largest bank. He also owns shares in Gazprom and VTB.
He headed Gazprom's office in Hungary for a while.
forbes_facts: Before his return to Russia in 2008 he was the richest person in Hungary.
His sons Timur and Ruslan are citizens of Hungary.
